newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO takes Deng's death in its stride.
newsitem.headline: NATO takes Deng's death in its stride.

text.p: Diplomats at NATO, which has no formal dealings with China, took the death of Deng Xiaoping calmly on Thursday, saying it was not unexpected and unlikely to have any impact in the alliance's main European sphere of influence.
"China is not really on our radar screen," said one official, but added NATO's leading members would clearly be monitoring future events in the country very closely.
There was no official, on-the-record comment from the alliance.
China opposes NATO's plans to expand eastwards, but far less stridently than Moscow. NATO sources said they expected no policy change on that front following Deng's death.
"They apparently fear a by-product of enlargement will be a permanent NATO-Russia link which could result in a large northern bloc ranged against them," said one diplomatic source.

However, he added most of China's hostility to NATO was a legacy of its hard-line communist past when the organisation was seen as a military club of western capitalist states and enlargement was not one of the leadership's top concerns.
The Western powers have supported Deng's economic reform programme, but regretted the leadership's refusal to sanction democratic reforms.
